newsitem.title: CHINA: Central bank selling hits yuan in Shanghai trade.
newsitem.headline: Central bank selling hits yuan in Shanghai trade.

text.p: Central bank selling weakened the yuan on Friday, keeping it below the key level of 8.2900 to the dollar and undermining its recently bullish tone, dealers said.
The local currency ended slightly lower at 8.2905 against 8.2903 on Thursday.

Trading was thin ahead of the weekend but dealers said that the failure to breach the 8.2900 level convincingly could hurt sentiment next week. Buyers tried to push the unit through the 8.2900 level several times this week but intervention by the central bank kept the yuan from firming significantly.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2903.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2903 and moved in a narrow band between an intraday high of 8.2901 and 8.2905 for most of the session. It touched a low of 8.2909.
"Yuan buyers may give up the battle with the central bank for the time being," said a dealer.
"The intervention by the central bank hurt yuan sentiment and attracted some follow-through yuan offers," he said.
